item.title: HUL hikes prices of detergent brands Surf Excel, Rin, Wheel by up to 11%
item.description: Hindustan Unilever has raised prices of Surf Excel, Rin and Wheel detergent products by up to 11%, with increases of ₹1-10 across pack sizes amid continued input cost pressures.
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: Hindustan Unilever has raised the maximum retail prices of several products across its home care portfolio, including popular detergent brands Surf Excel, Rin and Wheel, by up to 11 per cent, amid continued cost pressures and efforts to protect margins. Last month, MD and CEO Priya Nair said Hindustan Unilever Ltd (HUL) will continue to take calibrated price hikes depending on the movement in input costs, as elevated commodity inflation poses a challenge even as demand remains resilient. The price revisions cover multiple pack sizes, with increases ranging from Rs 1 to Rs 10. The company has raised the MRP of Surf Excel Quick Wash (1 kg pack) by Rs 10 to Rs 245 from Rs 235, and its 500-gram pack has become costlier by Rs 5 to Rs 128 from Rs 123. The price of Surf Excel Easy Wash (1 kg pack) has been increased by Rs 5 to Rs 172 from Rs 167, and the 500-gram pack now costs Rs 87 against Rs 85 earlier. The MRP of Surf Excel bar (250 gm) were raised by Rs 3 to Rs 45, while the four-bar bundle (200 gm each) has become costlier by Rs 10 to Rs 155. HUL has also increased prices of its Rin and Wheel products. The price of Rin Ala 500 ml has been raised by Rs 5 to Rs 95, and Rin detergent powder 1 kg and 500 gm packs have become costlier by Rs 3 and Rs 2, respectively, to Rs 123 and Rs 63. The company has raised the price of Wheel detergent powder 1 kg by Rs 3 to Rs 93, and its 500 gm pack now costs Rs 47 against Rs 46 earlier. Besides home care products, HUL has also raised the MRP of Moti Gulab soap (150 gm) by Rs 8 to Rs 82 from Rs 74, marking an increase of over 10 per cent. The latest revisions come at a time when FMCG companies are recalibrating prices across product categories to manage input cost inflation, while seeking to maintain volume growth in a competitive market.

item.description: Brent crude fell over 5 per cent to $93.27 a barrel after Trump signalled fresh strikes on Iran were unlikely if peace talks progressed, despite shipping attacks near Hormuz ...

Home / World News / Oil prices slide over 5% as Trump signals no fresh Iran strikes amid talks

Oil prices slide over 5% as Trump signals no fresh Iran strikes amid talks Brent crude fell over 5 per cent to $93.27 a barrel after Trump signalled fresh strikes on Iran were unlikely if peace talks progressed, despite shipping attacks near Hormuz

Reuters London 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 09 2026 | 11:43 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Brent crude futures hit their lowest level since early September on Monday after US President Donald Trump downplayed the likelihood of renewed strikes on Iran, though attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz kept supply concerns in focus.   Trump said on Sunday that he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progressed, even as both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz.   Brent crude futures were down $5.05, or 5.2 per cent, to $93.27 a barrel by 1427 GMT, having slid as low as $93.21 a barrel earlier.

US West Texas Intermediate lost $4.12, or 4.5 per cent, to $86.71 a barrel.   The Brent benchmark plunged 16 per cent last week to touch a two-month low of $93.22, marking its steepest weekly drop since the start of the Covid-19 pandemic. Also Read

The G2 illusion

From Trump to Bill Ackman: Reactions to Nvidia's probe into CEO Huang

"Oil continues to trade lower on hopes of a US-Iran peace deal rather than concrete signs of progress," said Saxo Bank analyst Ole Hansen, adding that Trump's latest comments that fresh strikes on Iran are highly unlikely have increased pressure on prices.   UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said: "Weakness in the physical market, supported by still-elevated flows out of the Middle East, is one factor weighing on prices."

Dated Brent, used to price cargoes around the world, has weakened to a discount to the nearby Brent futures contract, Morgan Stanley said in a report on Monday, highlighting weakness in the physical market.   Trump had hinted at a resumption of attacks on Iran after last week's US midterm elections, but there has been no sign of a large-scale US military operation. Iran has said it would respond by striking US and Israeli targets.   Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, called Trump's comments "more measured" but said the market is still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump's approach to the conflict or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.

The global oil market is showing signs of a return to excess supply as demand drops because of high prices, some analysts say. JP Morgan estimated a global oil surplus of 1.4 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, the bank said in a report last week.

Home / Markets / News / Nvidia's shares slide as chip giant probes CEO Huang over spy claims

Nvidia's shares slide as chip giant probes CEO Huang over spy claims Nvidia's shares tumbled more than 6% in Frankfurt trading, extending last week's selloff and pushing the stock to fresh multi-month lows

Nvidia shares fell sharply on Monday. (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 09 2026 | 10:39 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Nvidia shares fell sharply on Monday after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.   The internal probe ??followed a media report that Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who allegedly passed information to Beijing. Huang told Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship.   The investigation, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

The leather-jacketed Huang enjoys rock-star status worldwide, particularly in Asia, where he often mingles freely with fans, taking selfies and signing autographs for his devoted followers.   The fallout from the probe extended to South Korea, where Madison Huang, Huang's daughter and an Nvidia executive, cancelled a planned visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference that was set to begin on Monday, according to companies she had been scheduled to meet.   Also Read

How a hedge fund's warning against Nvidia gained relevance six months later

From Nvidia to Micron: Major China-linked espionage cases under scrutiny

Nvidia CEO Huang probe: China calls 'spy narrative' unsubstantiated

Chinese newspaper dismisses Nvidia CEO Huang spy claim, warns on ties

Jensen Huang is bigger than Nvidia, and that spells trouble for AI

Nvidia's shares tumbled more than 6% in Frankfurt trading, extending last week's selloff and pushing the stock to fresh multi-month lows. At those levels, the chipmaker stood to lose about $270 billion from its closing price on Friday, according to LSEG Datastream.

"The market's probably telling you now this does no favours to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build-out of data centres," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne. But Weston said he did not think Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", would be replaced. "If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down - it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest," he said.   The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

"The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.   Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Singapore. Alice Huang did not respond to the New York Times last month when it first reported her relationship with Huang, and Reuters could not determine her location to seek comment on Monday.   ASIA PARTNERS UNAFFECTED   Shares in Nvidia's key Asian chip suppliers TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rebounded on Monday after last week's selloff of AI-related stocks. TSMC shares jumped 6.5%, while those in Samsung and SK Hynix climbed 2.9% and 4.7%, respectively.

Some prominent figures weighed in on Huang's admission. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, said on X that the Nvidia CEO was an "incredible human," but if "indeed this is more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem."   "I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security," he added.   Tesla CEO Elon Musk commented, "I agree", on a post by Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire that said Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that was "bad ??for America" but that "Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership". US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had not spoken to Huang about the allegations, but called him a fine person. "I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job," he added.

When asked if he believed he should have acted on intelligence when he was briefed about it, Trump said: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it." The New York Times reported that Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings roughly a year ago and chose not to do anything with the information.   CANCELLED VISIT   Madison Huang had initially planned to visit South Korean AI startup Rebellions and hold a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said the events were cancelled due to "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia."

Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to draw about 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, will proceed as planned, according to South Korean media. Nvidia did not respond immediately to a request for comment.   Analysts said a prolonged investigation or internal review could potentially delay Nvidia's investment decisions or product launches, with broader implications for the semiconductor industry.   Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, said Nvidia's rivals, including Advanced Micro Devices, could attract greater attention in the short term, potentially putting Samsung, which has close business ties with AMD, in the spotlight.

Still, he said Nvidia's products would be difficult to replace, limiting the potential impact, although shipments to China could face further delays depending on how the situation developed.   South Korea's deputy science minister said on Monday the government expected no disruptions to contracted deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units despite issues currently facing the company.   (Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)   More From This Section

item.title: Bill Gates says billionaires should pay more taxes as AI reshapes economy
item.description: Gates said that governments must take primary responsibility for tackling inequality as AI generates wealth, warning that philanthropy cannot replace public support systems ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Technology / Tech News / Bill Gates says billionaires should pay more taxes as AI reshapes economy

Bill Gates says billionaires should pay more taxes as AI reshapes economy Gates said that governments must take primary responsibility for tackling inequality as AI generates wealth, warning that philanthropy cannot replace public support systems

Gates also highlighted the need to reconsider how governments tax labour and capital as businesses increasingly adopt AI tools and automation | Image: Bloomberg

Apexa Rai New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 09 2026 | 1:49 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has called for governments to reconsider taxation policies and ensure that billionaires and wealthy individuals contribute more towards addressing inequality, as the rapid growth of artificial intelligence(AI) threatens to widen the gap between rich and poor.   Speaking on the Financial Times' Tech Tonic podcast, Gates said governments must take primary responsibility for tackling economic inequality, rather than relying on charitable contributions from wealthy individuals.   "The primary responsibility of dealing with inequality will always rest with governments. We can't expect philanthropy, which is voluntary in nature, to be the safety net," Gates said.   He argued that tax systems would need to adapt to an economy increasingly shaped by AI , including ensuring that people with substantial wealth and billionaires contribute towards public welfare.

The comments come amid growing concerns that the economic gains from AI could remain concentrated among technology companies, investors and wealthy individuals, even as automation changes the nature of employment across industries. Also Read

Gates also highlighted the need to reconsider how governments tax labour and capital as businesses increasingly adopt AI tools and automation. Existing tax structures, he said, can make investment in machines more financially attractive than employing people.   In an essay published on his website, Gates Notes, he had previously proposed taxing robots, arguing that automation could otherwise accelerate job displacement without generating equivalent contributions towards public finances.   The Microsoft co-founder believes governments could use tax revenues to support workers affected by technological changes.

Gates, who has pledged to give away virtually all his wealth through the Gates Foundation over the next two decades, maintains that charitable giving cannot substitute for government-funded welfare and public services.
